Chapter 04 of 19

The Skytrain

CommuteTransit system / the elevated line90 BPM
The story

Terminal City has a lot of clocks, and none of them agree. So the city keeps its time by the SkyTrain. The trains run above the streets on a schedule no printed timetable matches, and every district sets its clocks by the sound of them passing overhead.

The trains carry passengers, but they also carry the day. A version of the morning's instructions rides on every train, loaded on by the Morning Mist, and it is delivered wherever the doors slide open. When a train is late, a whole district runs on yesterday. When two trains pass each other, their versions compare notes.

The crows inspect the guideway from above. The Old Line, which is older and more stubborn, refuses to speak to the SkyTrain at all. And late at night the Sixth Hour depends on the last train not really being the last. Set your clock by the train, not the clock.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
